title: Biliary Colic: Assessment and Discharge Criteria

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult with suspected biliary colic or gallstone disease: liver function tests and ultrasound, surgical referral, acute cholecystitis, bile duct stones and dietary advice, using NICE CG188. Analgesia and discharge thresholds are not covered by the source.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: NICE CG188 as extracted contains no analgesia, antiemetic or antibiotic advice or doses, no pancreatitis content, and no explicit red-flag or discharge criteria; local emergency department protocols apply.
Only recommendation 1.1.1 was numbered in the extract, so sections are cited.
No Saudi surgical guideline was opened.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: NICE offers liver function tests and ultrasound to people with suspected gallstone disease. Laparoscopic cholecystectomy is offered to people with symptomatic gallbladder stones; asymptomatic stones in a normal gallbladder and biliary tree need no treatment. Acute cholecystitis is treated with early laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 1 week of diagnosis. Bile duct stones, symptomatic or not, need duct clearance and cholecystectomy, by surgery or by endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP).

clinicalManagement.title: Classify
actions: Symptomatic gallbladder stones, acute cholecystitis, or bile duct stones.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer for surgery
actions: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy, day case where possible; within 1 week for acute cholecystitis.

clinicalManagement.title: Clear bile duct stones
actions: Surgical clearance at cholecystectomy or ERCP before or at the time; temporary stent only if ERCP fails.

clinicalManagement.title: Advise
actions: Avoid trigger foods and drinks until stones are removed; see the GP if symptoms persist afterwards.
